pairs.relationship: internal abuse report and stated example
pairs.rationale: The word 'other' continues the abuse already attributed to the men holding Jesus: they mock and beat Him, blindfold Him and demand that He identify His striker. These are the stated speakers and recorded example; the link does not reconstruct the many additional unquoted blasphemies.

The continuation 'and said to them' supplies Pilate's speech to the summoned chief priests, rulers and people: he reports his examination and Herod's result and proposes punishment and release. It identifies the purpose and recipients of this summons, without merging a different hearing or claiming that the proposed release was carried out.

deferred.reason: The Matthat-Levi-Melchi-Jannai-Joseph sequence is printed as this part of Luke's lineage. The nearby Matthew chain does not repeat it, and recurrent Levi or Joseph names do not establish identities or a missing genealogical bridge.

Mattathias-Amos-Nahum-Esli-Naggai is an ancestral chain, with no stated offices or deeds identifying these men. Names Amos and Nahum alone do not identify the prophetic authors, and no matching ordered chain has been established.

The Maath-Mattathias-Semein-Josech-Joda chain supplies names and descent only. The repeated Mattathias name in the larger list does not merge the men or connect either one with a separately named historical figure; no specific supported target is retained.
Melchi-Addi-Cosam-Elmadam-Er remains a distinct printed lineage segment. Repeated names elsewhere do not reproduce these ordered relationships or authorize an identity for an individual ancestor.

The ancestor named Jesus is followed by Eliezer-Jorim-Matthat-Levi in the printed chain. His name does not identify him with Jesus Christ or permit replacement by another form of the name; the repeated Matthat and Levi names do not establish a matching external chain.

Simeon-Judah-Joseph-Jonam-Eliakim is the actual ordered segment. Familiar patriarchal or royal names alone do not identify these ancestors, and the reread Matthew sequence does not supply the same relationships.
